key_insight: A target-domain adapted ensemble better predicted sustained antibiotic exposure in ICU patients with intracerebral hemorrhage when moved from MIMIC-IV to eICU, outperforming a source-only model.
clinical_relevance: This could help ICU teams identify patients with ICH who are more likely to receive prolonged antibiotics, supporting benchmarking, resource planning, and retrospective care analysis across hospitals.
method: Trained models on MIMIC-IV ICH ICU stays and adapted them to eICU data.
Combined 16 model probabilities with clinical, availability, and measurement-density features in a logistic meta-learner.
Used cross-fitting and a held-out eICU evaluation set to test transfer performance.
evidence_signal: On the held-out eICU subset (511 stays; 48 positive cases), the adapted ensemble reached AUROC 0.841 and AP 0.540, improving over the MIMIC-IV source-only stack AUROC of 0.782.
watch_item: The outcome is based on antibiotic exposure patterns, which may reflect local practice differences and documentation/measurement intensity rather than infection alone, so external deployment should be validated carefully.
paper_title: Cross-database adaptation of machine learning models for predicting sustained antibiotic exposure among patients with intracerebral hemorrhage in intensive care units
